title: Al-Mutaffifin: the rust on hearts
hook: what they earned has rusted over their hearts (83:14)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-Mutaffifin, and the two rulers, full for me, short for you. Your line was full measure. Where did you give the full amount? Day two hundred nine.

Leave a bike out in the rain for one night and nothing happens. Leave it out all winter and you come back to a chain that won't turn. Rust doesn't arrive in a day. It comes a speck at a time, each speck too small to bother with, until the thing just doesn't move anymore. Yesterday Al-Mutaffifin talked about skimming, the tiny cheat repeated. Today it explains what that repetition does, not to the customer, but to the one doing it. And it uses a picture anyone who's owned something metal will recognize. Today: the rust on hearts.
screen: `ONE NIGHT IN THE RAIN.` → `A WHOLE WINTER.` → `THE RUST ON HEARTS.`

segments.voice: The surah describes people who, when its verses are recited to them, say: stories of the ancients. Old tales, nothing to do with me. And verse fourteen explains why, in Pickthall's words: Nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts. The Arabic word is rana, a covering, a film, a crust that forms over something and dulls it. It isn't that they can't hear. It's that what they've done has built up, layer on layer, until the heart doesn't catch the light anymore. A hadith in Tirmidhi turns the verse into a picture. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said that when a person does wrong, a black spot is put on the heart. If he stops, asks forgiveness and turns back, the heart is polished clean. If he goes back to it, the spot grows, until it covers the heart. And that, he said, is the rana that God mentions. So the picture has two halves, and that's today's line. Hearts rust. And hearts shine. The rust isn't permanent unless you let it become so. Turning back, tawbah, is the polish. So is remembrance of God, which many scholars describe as the heart's cleaning cloth. Notice how it connects to yesterday. The man skimming a pinch off every sale doesn't feel like a villain. Each pinch is a speck. But the specks add up, not only in the ledger but in him, until the verses sound like old stories. And the surah goes on, a few verses later, to describe the other record, of the righteous, and says: for this, let those who compete, compete.
screen: `STORIES OF THE ANCIENTS.` · `RANA — A CRUST THAT DULLS.` · `A BLACK SPOT, OR POLISHED CLEAN.` · `LET THOSE WHO COMPETE, COMPETE.` · then, large: `HEARTS RUST; HEARTS SHINE.`

segments.voice: For two minutes, think of one small habit that's been building up quietly. A little dishonesty, a daily irritation you feed, a thing you keep meaning to stop. Just one speck. Picture it as a spot on something that should shine. Then picture a cloth, and one slow wipe. If you pray, you can say astaghfirullah, I seek God's forgiveness. The bell holds the time.
Al-Mutaffifin. Those who skim, Surah eighty-three, which says what they earned became rust on their hearts. Today's word.
Your line: hearts rust; hearts shine. Polish one habit today: stop it once, and notice the shine that comes back. Day two hundred nine.

howItsDone: Muslims speak of polishing the heart through tawbah, turning back, and dhikr, remembrance; many say astaghfirullah often through the day, recalling the hadith of the black spot that is wiped clean.

fork.setup: a black spot has been put on a heart by a wrong. according to the hadith, what cleans it?
options: stopping, asking forgiveness and turning back
doing twice as many good deeds first
fork.reveal: if he stops, asks forgiveness and turns back, the heart is polished (Tirmidhi). if he returns to it, the spot grows.

original.note: Arabic: "covered over, rusted," a crust that dulls a surface (Qur'an 83:14).

trapdoor: what you thought: bad deeds make a bad heart.
what it means: small wrongs repeated form a crust over the heart until even the verses sound like old stories; turning back polishes it.

what a scholar hears: rana, ghayn and tab' are degrees of covering the scholars distinguish; Tirmidhi 3334 is the hadith of the black spot; asatir al-awwalin, tales of the ancients, is a recurring Meccan dismissal in the Qur'an.

sources.quoted: Nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts.

sources.ref: Qur'an 83:13, 83:18–26 (stories of the ancients; the record of the righteous; let those who compete, compete)
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3334; Sunan Ibn Majah 4244 (the black spot on the heart)

notes: Please confirm the exact Pickthall wording of 83:14.
Tirmidhi 3334 / Ibn Majah 4244 cited from memory; confirm numbers and wording.
rana / ghayn / tab' as degrees of covering is a scholarly distinction (e.g. in Ibn al-Qayyim); confirm or drop.
Remembrance as the heart's polish is attributed generally to 'many scholars'; a hadith to that effect (in al-Bayhaqi) is weak and not cited.
